comparable_reason: The outputs split cleanly and I re-measured both halves on 51 archived models with resolvable HF configs. The HT-SR exponent IS comparable, being dimensionless by construction: avg_alpha_official rho(d_model) = +0.1799 (p = 0.21) and rho(n_layers) = +0.1686 (p = 0.24); avg_alpha (the Hill proxy) is -0.0237 (p = 0.87) and +0.0151 (p = 0.92). avg_stable_rank is NOT comparable: rho(d_model) = +0.8885 (p = 3.4e-18), rho(log params) = +0.9185 (p = 2.2e-21), rho(n_layers) = +0.7149 (p = 3.8e-09), and it is structurally bounded above by min(m, n). avg_alpha_hat = alpha * log10(lambda_max) multiplies the dimensionless exponent by a scale-dependent norm and lands in between (+0.2776 / +0.2911, p ~ 0.04-0.05). The strongest association for the alpha family is with VOCABULARY -- avg_alpha_official rho(vocab) = +0.7380 (p = 6.5e-10) and avg_alpha +0.6599 (p = 1.4e-07) -- which in this zoo is essentially a model-family label rather than a mechanism (a fresh 10-model panel gave exactly 0.000 for the same pair in the prior round). So: comparable for the alpha family with a family caveat, not comparable for stable rank.

paper_reason: Martin, Peng & Mahoney (Nat Commun 12:4122, arXiv 2002.06716) Table 2 gives GPT2-small: 49 layers treated, weighted alpha (alpha_hat) = 9.62. The current code reports avg_alpha_hat = 11.100879024732404 on its own 49-module population (+15.4%) and 10.942422 over the 48 Conv1D modules alone (+13.7%). The gap is NOT BLME's estimator: on WeightWatcher's own 49-module population BLME gives 10.832650 against live weightwatcher 0.7.7's 10.833166, i.e. it reproduces the CURRENT released reference to 4.8e-05 while the current reference itself sits +12.6% above the 2020 published value. That residual is reference-version drift between the paper's `powerlaw`-package fitter and WWFit; WW's pl_package='powerlaw' path is not runnable here (the `powerlaw` dependency is unavailable and the path returns alpha = -1.0), so the last 12.6% cannot be closed locally.
confounds_reason: For avg_stable_rank the confound is confirmed and its mechanism is structural: stable rank = ||W||_F^2 / ||W||_2^2 is bounded above by min(m, n), and it measures rho(d_model) = +0.8885 (p = 3.4e-18, n = 51), rho(log params) = +0.9185 (p = 2.2e-21) and rho(n_layers) = +0.7149 (p = 3.8e-09). For the alpha family the architecture association is null (avg_alpha_official +0.1799 / +0.1686, avg_alpha -0.0237 / +0.0151), so those columns are not size proxies; their large vocabulary correlation (+0.7380 and +0.6599) is a model-family effect in this zoo, not a mechanical one.
